text: Simple yet thoughtful enough that you can identify quality game design is present here regardless of having experience with the developers previous works or not. Stands alone as a great old school/boomer shooter with satisfying gunplay and tight level design. At such a low price just grab this one

I got this game a week or two after it's early access release, played it with friends and loved it. I would go as far to say this is up there with some of my favourite games of all time, it's great fun with a good group of friends and the variation between levels means it doesn't get old. 100% recommend getting this game, even more so with friends.

With the full release I look forward to playing it again :D

An amazing developer - I absolutely love their games. I would recommend their titles to any fan of Metroidvanias and relaxing games with great storytelling. They exude such a peaceful atmosphere, and you can instantly feel the heart and passion poured into them. The storylines, dialogue, music, and enemy variety all deserve special recognition, reflecting the incredible effort invested in every project. I eagerly await future releases and wish the team continued success.
Nothing world changing. Just a solid metroidvania game involving dinosaurs and aliens

The gameplay is cool, the world is interesting and the characters are cute, however, I don't think this game is worth $40, I've finished the game in around 4 hours and for that content the price shouldn't go above $20-$25. The fact that season pass is being released for an additional $25, worth probably 3-4 hours of gameplay is pretty unrealistic as well. Oh and not to mention the fact that I've disconnected few times in the game and it was a bit buggy, nothing too bad but the player experience could be better. I'd recommend to buy this game when it's on sale, it will probably be worth the price then.

Best Resident Evil game of all time!!!

I can't remember the last time a game kept me so much focused into it. I loved it so much that i decided to go for all the achievements and I can't describe the satisfaction I got when i got the last one. I recommend this game to absolutely anyone. I played lots of Resident Evil games and lots of horror games but there is not a single game that comes close to this one imo.

Just get the game, you wil totally love it!

Fantastic game. Definitely my favorite indie metroidvania.
The difficulty is a bit on the harder side in terms of combat, but the exploration is made to be easy.
The controls are responsive, and the platforming feels great. 
The art and music are fun and fit with the setting.
Absolutely worth a play.

Shadow of the Tomb Raider offers the best game of the trilogy. While the jungle might be a place of death, the game really comes to life with a nice balance of puzzles, combat and exploring. A true ending to a awesome trilogy.

It might be kinda old. It might be arguably past its prime. And I may just be autistic and this game might be one of my special interests. But this game slaps.
This game is a classic for me. One of the prime games of growing up on the weird fandom side of the internet. I love the simplicities AND the complexities of it. It's pattern recognition yet it keeps you guessing. The depth of the storyline had me in a chokehold from the first time I cared to pay attention to it. The character designs are interesting. I love this stupid little indie horror game. 10/10.

For South Park fans: It is a 11-hour interactive episode of South Park that you would enjoy if you like the crude humor from South Park, definitely worth purchasing.

Positive points:
+ This is a light RPG with few status effects and simple combat.
+ The story is extreme to say the least.
+ Four classes to choose from, each with different play styles.
+ Interesting achievements.

Negative points:
- Balance is skewed towards being too easy.
- Glitchy at times.
- Locked at 30FPS. (not really an issue but still a worthy note)
- Steam version is censored. (Australian, EU or German versions that I am aware of)

I absolutely loved my time in this game and it was a treat to finish. The game has a demo and I think that is an excellent way to see if the game is for you so I do recommend trying the demo. 

I really enjoyed the gameplay, just moving through the zones felt great. The atmosphere and music were absolutely top notch and it did tonal shifts absolutely masterfully. Crawling through blood and guts, everything seeming just depressing, dark and cruel and I start to get the feeling this game is just a dark dark game and nothing else but then suddenly I am in a beautiful forest with the most amazing tranquil music playing. 

Highly recommend.

A very unique online co-op story driven game from Hazelight. I haven't played anything like A Way Out before. The game heavily relies on co-operation of two players in order to advance throughout the entire story. Sure the game might feel outdated in terms of mechanics and AI but it was released back in 2018. Still, I believe it doesn't really have any competitors in its own league.

If you are the type of person that enjoys story driven games but also find the idea of playing this game with your friends, then best time to grab A Way Out is during a sale!

Note: You only need 1 copy of the game to be able to play with one of your friends. The person that owns the full game can give access to another person of the full game via an in-game invite. The other person only has to download the trial version.
What a beautiful piece of art. From the animation to the story to the music. If this does not elicit an emotional response from you, you might be dead inside.

This was a good remake. Not a 1-for-1 remake - so it was still fun to figure out new routes/puzzles - but enough of the old to appreciate the updated textures and physics. Zen was done well, but got a little long.  I'd appreciate a remake of Blue Shift and Opposing Force next, followed by HL2.

As someone who is as obsessed with Sentai/Tokesatsu/KamenRider/PowerRangers as he is with Megaman/RetroActionPlatformers, I would like to tell Domesticated Ant Games:

Thank you for developing this masterpiece. I know you didn't make it just for me, but it sure as hell felt like it.

Playing this in VR and it is quite the experience. I wouldn't call it a walking sim like Firewatch, there's more to it than that, but it's not a fast paced game.  The art is amazing and the atmosphere is engrossing in VR.  I have to give compliments to the devs for making the game playable either flatscreen or in VR, I wish more games included an option for VR, as it truly is the most immersive way to experience a game and modern headsets are quite good

Just dive into it. If any advice, don't focus on those "collectibles" because they break an otherwise perfect immersion. To my own surprise, I went through the whole game in one playthrough, without a break. Couldn't take a break. It takes you to some very old and forgotten places, and some you hopefully don't know anything about (yet). The absence of UI, of character enhancement, of written tips makes you forget it's a game. You're just following (and often merging with) Senua. It was litterally breath taking, multiple times. But. This game is only for you if you're willing to dive in a unique experience rather than actually play a game, if you're willing to let yourself be Senua and not think you can just beat everything because, well, it's a game after all.

While Alien Isolation is a perfect homage to first Alien movie, Dark Descent is the same thing for sequel Aliens. It is as loyal to the source material as it can get. Setting, visuals, sounds, music, everything is a pure bliss for Aliens fan. It is basically XCOM game, but instead of turn-based combat, everything is realtime, and it makes every encounter very tense and very often leads to similar hopeless situations as seen in the movie. Now I only hope that sometime in the future we will also get a sequel.

Just finished Titanfall 2… and damn, I wasn’t expecting it to hit this hard.

At first I thought it’s just another shooter, but the way the story builds up, the missions, the gameplay twists… everything feels so fresh. And BT… bro that wasn’t just a machine, it actually felt like a real companion.
The ending really got me. Like you just sit there for a minute thinking about it… didn’t feel like a game ending, felt like losing someone.
Honestly, games like this are rare now.
Glad I played this.

The core combat mechanics feel good, but the game is unacceptably broken. There are a couple of really good bosses that I enjoyed a lot, but most are somewhere between barely bosses, and so bad I can't believe they made it into the game in the state that they are in.

Here is a great example of the game not being ready for prime time. If about a third of the time that you die, your souls just don't spawn to give you a chance to be pick them up, your game is not ready to ship. That is THE souls mechanic in a souls-like, and if you can't do that extremely basic core mechanic consistently, go make something else please.

I do have a feeling that if the devs keep working to fix the insane amount of bugs and revamp some of the extremely boring fights, like the final boss, this could be a great game in 6 months. Until then play a better, less broken video game.

Not bad! Not exactly top tier in this genre, but a respectable entry. The combat feels pretty solid, even if there isn't a huge roster of enemies and bosses. Platforming is also fun, with a somewhat unique gimmick with the "Aether Lamps", that let you create your own jump pads, of a sort. I like this because it makes tough platforming challenges into more of a puzzle that has to be worked out, rather than the solution being obvious and simply requiring precise mechanical execution. I like the art direction as well, though I'd say that is one of the games major flaws. The environments are nice, but a bit too cluttered, making it hard to navigate by sight alone, making one over-reliant on the mini-map for clarity. But overall, a solid experience, and one I'd recommend to fans of Metroidvanias.

Phenomenal sequel to the Planet of Lana Series. Very compelling story and beautiful art direction. A couple of more challenging puzzles this time is the addition of some fun mechanics. The tone felt darker this time which I personally enjoy a lot. Increasing the stakes narratively with a great payoff at the end. Highly recommend!
